members.title: Thursday briefing: Why young people are taking to the streets across France
French high school protests continue despite PM’s promise of action – Europe live
members.lead: High school protests across France show no sign of slowing down, with nearly 400 educational establishments facing disruptions this morning. Demonstrators have rejected a promise by prime minister Sébastien Lecornu to present a plan to fix the country’s education system by the end of the month, demanding he fully engages with their demands sooner than that. In a televised address last night, Lecornu said the country could not be “indifferent” to their concerns, and acknowledged that their anger “does not come from nowhere,” but did not make any immediate headline-grabbing announcements. “We want real action, and until we get it, we’ll keep mobilising,” a high school student named Marilou in Fontainebleau told AFP. I will keep an eye on today’s events in France as they unfold. Over in Spain, I will look at reactions after last night’s death of María del Carmen Abascal, the 87-year-old whose eviction set off a nationwide wave of protests against Spain’s housing crisis.
